stories.title: Staff stay signed in all shift: silent single-flight token refresh with returnTo
stories.story: As a doctor I want my session to refresh silently in the background so that I never lose a half-written note or Rx to a forced logout.
stories.context: The backend issues 15-minute access tokens (application.yml:59) and 30-day rotating refresh tokens (POST /v1/auth/refresh, old token invalidated on use). The clinic app never calls refresh: ~20 copies of authedFetch treat 401 as 'remove token, router.replace(/login)'. app/platform/platformApi.ts:22-49 already does single-flight refresh correctly; port it. Because refresh tokens rotate, two tabs refreshing at once would trip reuse detection (sessions.family_id revoke) and log the user out everywhere, so refresh must be single-flight across tabs (Web Locks API `navigator.locks.request('nabd-refresh')` plus a BroadcastChannel that hands the new token to other tabs). Refresh proactively at 80% of `exp` and reactively on 401. If refresh truly fails, store a same-origin `returnTo` path (validated, never an absolute URL) and bring the user back after re-login. The idle-lock unlock call must refresh first, so an expired token is no longer reported as 'Incorrect PIN'. This is an interim client-side fix; FEF-009 moves tokens into httpOnly cookies.
acceptance: Given a doctor signed in at 08:00, when a scripted 8 h shift makes requests every 1-5 minutes across 3 tabs, then there are 0 redirects to /login and 0 reuse-detected revocations
Given 6 requests that all receive 401 at the same moment, when the client handles them, then exactly one POST /v1/auth/refresh is sent and all 6 requests are retried once with the new token
Given two tabs whose access tokens expire together, when both need a token, then only one tab calls refresh and the other receives the rotated token over BroadcastChannel within 500 ms

Given the refresh token is revoked (admin revoke or 30-day expiry), when the next request fails refresh, then the user lands on /login?returnTo=<current path> and after login returns to the same patient/visit page
Given a returnTo of `https://evil.example` or `//evil.example`, when login completes, then the user is sent to their role landing page instead

Given the idle lock is shown for 20 minutes, when the doctor enters the correct PIN, then the app refreshes first and unlocks; a wrong PIN shows 'Incorrect PIN', an expired session shows 'Session expired, sign in again' and a 429 shows 'Too many attempts, wait N s'

stories.title: Idle lock cannot be bypassed and leaves no readable drafts on shared workstations
stories.story: As a doctor on a shared consult-room PC I want the screen lock to hold across reload and tabs and my drafts to be unreadable after sign-out so that the next user cannot see my patients.
stories.context: IdleLockGuard keeps lock state in React state only (IdleLockGuard.tsx:18): F5 or a new tab removes it while the token is still valid. The page behind the 97%-opaque scrim is not inert, so Tab still reaches PHI controls; the PIN input has no label; the skip list drifted from SHELL_SKIP_PREFIXES. Consult drafts (nabd-consult-drafts IndexedDB, draftStore.ts:8) survive signOut() and the idle-lock sign-out in plaintext. Fix: persist `lockedAt` in sessionStorage+localStorage and broadcast lock/unlock over BroadcastChannel; set `inert` on the app root while locked; role=dialog aria-modal; per-tenant timeout from a clinic setting (default 5 min, range 2-30) with a 30 s warning countdown; on sign-out delete the drafts database; encrypt drafts with an AES-GCM key generated per session and held only in memory (non-extractable CryptoKey), so drafts left after a crash are unreadable. Reload while unlocked must keep the key (store a wrapped key in sessionStorage encrypted by a BFF-held secret after FEF-009; until then accept that a reload loses unrecoverable drafts and warn).

stories.title: Sessions move into httpOnly cookies behind an in-region same-origin BFF
stories.story: As a clinic owner accountable for patient data I want staff sessions held in httpOnly cookies behind our own domain so that a malicious script cannot steal a 30-day login.
stories.context: Access and 30-day refresh tokens sit in localStorage (login/page.tsx:45-46, accept-invite, owner/workspaces, account). The frontend is on Vercel and the API on Render, so they are cross-site. ADR-06: Next route handlers at /api/* act as a BFF, deployed in-region because PHI passes through it (Vercel keeps only public/static assets). The refresh token lives in `__Host-nabd_rt` (httpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict; Path=/), the access token in `__Host-nabd_at` (httpOnly, 15 min), and the BFF proxies /api/v1/* to Core with the Authorization header. The browser never sees a token. CSRF: Origin check plus double-submit `__Host-nabd_csrf` cookie echoed as X-CSRF-Token on non-GET. Operator console uses separate cookie names. SSE (/api/events) streams through the same BFF so EventSource gets cookie auth. CORS on Core becomes nearly moot (closes MF-49). proxy.ts does optimistic auth redirects for (clinic)/(platform)/(owner) route groups.
